entries.claim: The replacement broke a pronoun referent. Before, the text read "a `$ARGUMENTS` that isn't empty ... An empty one". Now it reads "With more than one design, this run's arguments that aren't empty go straight to ... An empty one writes nothing and ends on the which-design question". "One" no longer matches the plural "arguments", and the nearest singular noun is "design".
entries.failure_scenario: Two or more designs exist and the user runs a bare /seldon. The sentence that sends empty arguments to the which-design question now says "An empty one". It can be read as "an empty design" instead of empty arguments, which weakens the only line that sends a bare multi-design run to the which-design question. Wording such as "Empty arguments write nothing and end on the which-design question" would keep the referent.

entries.claim: The new test only checks that the token appears once and sits between the two marker lines. It does not check where the block is, so moving the whole three-line block anywhere in SKILL.md still passes, even though the prose at SKILL.md:53-61 says "the marker lines below" and "the block above". This was measured, not imagined. Note that the plan text itself states no placement requirement: the bar that a move must fail comes from this review's task.
entries.failure_scenario: Mutation run on an archive of commit 376eded: delete the `<seldon-arguments>` / `$ARGUMENTS` / `</seldon-arguments>` block from section 1 and append it at the end of SKILL.md, after </process>. `node --test tests/skill.test.mjs` still passes ('$ARGUMENTS appears once, on its own line inside the seldon-arguments markers' ok, fail 0). In the moved file, "Only the block above is" at line 61 points to a block that is no longer above it, so the test does not catch the move it was meant to guard against.
